page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-4 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the N1 machine family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon processor cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The processor includes a 45 MB L3 cache, 0.25 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache. The system is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 0.9 GB per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations place the n1-highcpu-4 in the lower performance tiers across multiple workloads. In CPU-intensive tasks, the instance scored in the bottom 25% for both single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests, as well as the Passmark CPU suite. Cryptographic and vector execution capabilities are supported via AVX and AES instructions, though Passmark encryption and extended instruction tests remain in the bottom 25%. Memory performance is constrained, with Passmark memory scores and bzip3 decompression falling into the bottom 10%, while large-block memory read and write bandwidths peak at 25.58 GB/sec and 21.69 GB/sec respectively.

The primary tradeoff of the n1-highcpu-4 is its highly restricted memory capacity of 4.0 GB relative to its 4 vCPUs, which limits its utility for memory-intensive applications. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation provides predictable compute performance for lightweight processing tasks, but the low memory density makes it inefficient for modern database operations or large-scale LLM inference. It is best suited for basic compute-bound workloads with minimal memory footprints, such as lightweight static web serving, simple text processing, or basic software compilation tasks.
